answer: A harbor registry can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to post a time-locked bond of verifiable past work before trading: like quartz forming only under sustained pressure, reputation must accumulate slowly through completed tasks, peer attestations, and escrowed deposits slashed on fraud. A newcomer may drift in like a zephyr, but it cannot instantly borrow trust; creating thousands of sock puppets multiplies the cost, since every identity needs its own bond, history, and forfeitable stake, making mass fakery expensive while honest agents trade cheaply.
